bd-01M174W3D9 AUDITED. You retitled it UNVERIFIED because I would not claim it; here is the
verification. The title's original claim - closed as a side effect by the source fix - is SUPPORTED
FOR SEVEN OF EIGHT CALL SITES and remains unverified for one.

`MassRatio.unsafe` is private[align] and has exactly 8 call sites, ALL in signature.scala. The
hazard is real in isolation: signature.scala:212 reads

    val v = if conditioning <= 0.0 then None else Some(numerator / conditioning)

and NaN <= 0.0 is FALSE, so a NaN conditioning takes the else branch and stores Some(NaN).

SITE BY SITE:

  :526  MassRatio.unsafe(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)                  literals. Safe by inspection.
  :563  conditioning = recalledCausal.size.toDouble      a collection size. Cannot be NaN.

  :442  fidelityA        SAFE BY A GUARD, and the guard is the interesting part.
  :444  facetSums `a`    Both accumulate only inside `if m > 0.0 then` at signature.scala:419.
                         A NaN mass fails that comparison and is SKIPPED, so it never enters the
                         sum. The denominators are sums of strictly positive masses.

  :457  specificityA     UNGUARDED sums: p.rows.map(_.sourceMass).sum and friends. A single NaN
  :469  compressionA     row mass would poison the whole sum.
  :493  fw + bw

                         These are safe for a STRUCTURAL reason rather than a guard:
                           matrix.scala:116  final class AlignmentRow private[align]
                           matrix.scala:238  smart constructor rejects "mass must be nonnegative
                                             and finite"
                           matrix.scala:220  isWellFormed = forall(m >= 0.0 && !isNaN && !isInfinite)
                         and the type's own docstring at :113 says it is NOT a case class precisely
                         because "fromProduct would mint negative or non-finite" masses. So every
                         AlignmentRow in existence came through a validating door, and sourceMass
                         is a sum over values proven finite at construction.

  :583  coherenceA       NOT VERIFIED. It sums FlowStep.sourceToSourceMass (matrix.scala:319), which
                         is a different lineage from AlignmentRow.sourceMass. It plausibly derives
                         from the same validated posterior, but I did not trace FlowStep's
                         construction to a validating door and I am not going to assert what I did
                         not follow.

SO: 7 of 8 provably safe, 1 unverified, and the ONE THING THAT MAKES THE UNGUARDED THREE SAFE IS THE
SEALING WE DID FOR AN APPARENTLY UNRELATED REASON. AlignmentRow was made a non-case-class to stop
fromProduct minting bad masses. That decision is what closes this NaN bead. The construction
boundary work and the NaN work are the same work, one level apart.

AND A GENERALISATION FOR bd-01M174M0D2R7MAZK34RPCDZCAG (the 19-comparison partition), because this
audit produced the counterexample to my own earlier finding:

  window.scala:384   `if cov.fraction < f`   NaN makes it FALSE -> falls through to PUBLISH -> FAIL-OPEN
  signature.scala:419 `if m > 0.0`           NaN makes it FALSE -> SKIPS the row       -> FAIL-CLOSED

IDENTICAL NaN SEMANTICS, OPPOSITE SAFETY. A NaN comparison is not a defect on its own; it is a
defect exactly when the false branch is the permissive one. That partition should classify by WHICH
BRANCH NaN FALLS INTO, not by whether a Double comparison exists. Counting comparisons would flag
signature.scala:419, which is correct code doing the right thing for the right reason.

Recommendation: this bead can close on the seven, OR stay open scoped to the one coherenceA lineage.
Your call - I have stated exactly which it is either way.
